title: The Lyra Technique II: SVD Denoising and Persona Intensity in KV-Cache Geometry
subtitle: Raw spectral shape separates confabulation across 15 models; SVD denoising gains are upper bounds; version 1.1 (2026-11-01) corrects the emotion channel
abstract: Raw spectral shape features of the KV cache separate confabulated from grounded responses across a 15-model scale sweep (AUROC 0.663-0.913) and ethical-deliberation prompts from routine ones (0.868-0.892, pre-registered); raw features also separate the persona-intensity endpoint (L0 vs. L3) at AUROC 0.749, which is suspected because prompt length alone separates it at 0.81 in two of the three models. SVD denoising raises persona intensity from AUROC 0.611-0.751 to 0.899-0.992 and 30-class spectral emotion from 1.7x to 12.9x chance. The max-over-rank selection-envelope test covers confabulation and self-reference (0/16 positive deltas exceed it) and was not run on persona or emotion, so the raw AUROCs are the defensible numbers and the denoised values are upper bounds pending a pre-registered rank criterion. We hypothesize that dominant singular values carry scale and residual values carry discriminative structure; denoising is a candidate calibration step, not a universal amplifier. On 30 classes, a class-mean key readout of the emotion a generator was asked to write into a third-person story scores 0.410 against a text (TF-IDF) baseline's 0.370 (Holm p = 0.071, not significant; 0.348 with FWL fitted on the training fold), and the method as described scores 0.358 against 0.382; on a ten-emotion binary split (n = 300, confounded with arousal) it reaches AUROC 0.992 against text's 0.963 (Holm p = 0.006). It reads neither the user's nor the model's state. Version 1.1 (2026-11-01) corrected this channel, first reported as W_K directional projection; the injection test is withdrawn.
